Order
This bail application is filed under section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').

2. Petitioner is the first accused in Crime No.1205/2024 of Balussery Police Station, Kozhikode District registered alleging offense punishable under sections 406, 420, 465 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code.

3. According to the prosecution, the accused had, induced the de-facto complainant to pay an amount of Rs.12,00,000/- for securing employment for his son-in-law in the Kerala State Beverages Corporation and thereafter, the accused issued false documents like interview card, appointment order., etc and cheated the de facto complainant and failed to return the amount so collected and thereby committed the offenses alleged.
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as the learned Public Prosecutor.
5. The learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that the prosecution allegations are false and the petitioner is not involved in the crime at all.

It was also submitted that the circumstances alleged by the defacto complainant are fabricated to falsely rope the petitioner as an accused and the allegations are only the machinations of the defacto complainant.

Petitioner, who claims to be a reputed person in the locality, will be seriously prejudice if custodial interrogation is carried out,
contended the learned counsel.

6. The learned Public Prosecutor, on the other hand, submitted that, in the very first instance itself,
the defacto complainant had pointed out the involvement of the petitioner, as is evident from FI Statement wherein reference is made to handing over of Rs.7,00,000/- to the petitioner who issued a forged interview letter.
It was further submitted that the petitioner evaded from responding to the defacto complainant on various occasions and hence custodial interrogation is necessary.

sentences.text:
The petitioner and other accused are alleged to 2025:KER:41239 have collected Rs.12,00,000/-
for providing an employment to the defacto complainant's son-in-law.
Specific reference has been made in the FI Statement regarding the role of the petitioner.
Forged letter of interview as well as forged appointment order are allegedly created at the behest of the petitioner.
Considering the nature of allegations, I am of the view that the custodial interrogation is necessary in a case of this nature.

8. In a recent decision in P. Krishna Mohan Reddy vs. State of Andra Pradesh (2025 LiveLaw SC 598) the Supreme Court had observed that custodial interrogation is qualitatively more elicitation oriented than questioning a suspect who is well ensconced with a favourable order of pre- arrest bail.

entities.text: P. Krishna Mohan Reddy vs. State of Andra Pradesh (2025 LiveLaw SC 598)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was also observed that success in interrogation will elude if the suspected person knows that he is well protected and insulated by a prearrest bail order during the time he is interrogated.
In fact, the court went on to hold that insulating a person from arrest would make his interrogation a mere ritual.
10. On a consideration of the entire circumstances, I am of the view that this is not a fit case where the petitioner 2025:KER:41239 can be protected within an order of pre-arrest bail.
Accordingly this bail application is dismissed.

Sd/-
